title: Ezekiel Bible Quiz - Chapter 28
description: Ten questions on Ezekiel 28: the word to the prince of Tyre, the lamentation over the king of Tyre, and the word against Sidon.

questions.text: What had the prince of Tyre said about himself?
questions.explanation: He said: I am a god, I sit in the seat of God, in the middle of the seas; yet, the chapter says, he is man and not God.

answers.text: That he would live for ever in the sea
That he is a god who sits in the seat of God
That he is the son of the god of the sea
That no sword of man can ever touch him

questions.text: Whom is the prince of Tyre said to be wiser than?
questions.explanation: The chapter says: behold, you are wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that is hidden from you.

answers.text: Than the kings of the east
Than the wise men of Egypt
Than the princes of the sea
Than Daniel

questions.text: How does the chapter say he had gathered gold and silver into his treasures?
questions.explanation: It says that by his wisdom and by his understanding he had gotten himself riches, and had gotten gold and silver into his treasures.

answers.text: By the tribute of the islands
By the plunder of many nations
By his wisdom and his understanding
By the gifts of other kings

questions.text: Whom would the Lord Yahweh bring against the prince of Tyre?
questions.explanation: He says he will bring strangers on him, the terrible of the nations, who will draw their swords against the beauty of his wisdom.

answers.text: Strangers, the terrible of the nations
The armies of Pharaoh of Egypt
The princes of Sidon and Arvad
His own servants and merchants

questions.text: How is the king of Tyre described at the start of the lamentation?
questions.explanation: The lamentation says: you were the seal of full measure, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty.

answers.text: As a shepherd of many peoples
As the seal of full measure, perfect in beauty
As a cedar with beautiful branches
As a monster in the middle of the seas

questions.text: Where does the lamentation say the king of Tyre had been?
questions.explanation: It says: you were in Eden, the garden of God, and every precious stone adorned you.

answers.text: In the city of Babylon
On the islands of Kittim
In Eden, the garden of God
In the land of Pathros

questions.text: What was he called in the lamentation, and where was he set?
questions.explanation: It says he was the anointed cherub who covers, and that he was set up on the holy mountain of God.

answers.text: A king of kings, set over the sea
A prince of peace, set in the temple
A mighty hunter, set in the forest
The anointed cherub, set on God's mountain

questions.text: Until when was he perfect in his ways, according to the lamentation?
questions.explanation: It says he was perfect in his ways from the day that he was created, until unrighteousness was found in him.

answers.text: Until unrighteousness was found in him
Until the strangers came against him
Until his riches were taken away
Until the fire came out of his sanctuaries

questions.text: Toward which city was the prophet told to set his face in the second half of the chapter?
questions.explanation: He was told to set his face toward Sidon and prophesy against it, and to say: behold, I am against you, Sidon.

answers.text: Toward the city of Memphis
Toward Sidon
Toward the city of Rabbah
Toward the city of Arvad

questions.text: To whose servant does the chapter say the land was given, where Israel would dwell again?
questions.explanation: It says that when he has gathered the house of Israel from the peoples, they will dwell in their own land, which he gave to his servant Jacob.

answers.text: To his servant Abraham
To his servant David
To his servant Jacob
To his servant Moses
